einzeiler: Dr. Louise Newson breaks down the truth about menopause, hormones, and HRT for women…
kurzfassung: Dr. Louise Newson explains why the vast majority of women are underserved by outdated medical guidelines regarding menopause. She debunks persistent myths surrounding HRT, breast cancer risks, and testosterone, emphasizing the importance of individualized hormone care. Additionally, she discusses how body-identical hormones support brain, bone, and cardiovascular health throughout a woman's life.
stichpunkte: Only a small percentage of menopausal women globally receive HRT despite guidelines recommending it as first-line treatment.
The 2002 study that scared a generation away from HRT used synthetic hormones and cannot be compared to modern body-identical treatments.
Testosterone is described as a vital female hormone that significantly impacts mood, energy, and muscle strength.
Vaginal and rectal progesterone delivery methods can help patients avoid side effects experienced with oral tablets.
Hormone deficiencies directly impact neurological function, contributing to symptoms often misdiagnosed as depression or anxiety.
Estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone all act as anti-inflammatory agents that support joint, bone, and skin health.
Lifestyle factors like diet and exercise are important, but they cannot replace declining hormone levels.
Patients are encouraged to seek second opinions and advocate for evidence-based menopause care.
beschreibung:
This week's Best of The Body Pod episode was selected for a rerun because menopause education is something our community keeps asking for, and Dr. Louise Newson's insights are just as essential today as when we first released this conversation. If you missed it the first time, or need a refresher, this is a powerful conversation that every woman over 40 needs to hear. In this game-changing episode, Dr. Louise Newson, known as "the medic who kickstarted the menopause revolution," joins us to debunk menopause myths, explain hormone therapy (HRT), and redefine what healthy aging looks like. We discuss:
Why too many women are wrongly prescribed antidepressants for perimenopause
The essential roles of estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone in brain, bone, and heart health
The real science behind HRT and who it's for
Why individualized, evidence-based care matters
The dangers of medical misinformation and outdated menopause narratives

Whether you're in perimenopause, postmenopause, or just starting to ask questions, this episode offers empowering, no-nonsense insights to help you make informed health decisions. Dr. Newson's message is clear: no woman should suffer through menopause without support, education, and choice.
